In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incorporation of the water droplet into the polystyrenes is strongly dependent on the experimental parameters used in the synthesis procedure.

a higher water content, smaller water droplet diameter and a higher stability of the water-in-oil dispersion can be obtained by using a lower HLB surfactant, a high-speed impeller, and a longer water dispersion phase.

the use of an appropriate surfactant with low HLB value and a short dispersion time can result in a high incorporation of water into polystyrene, which in turn results in an increased expansion ratio.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the incorporation of water into polystyrene is strongly influenced by experimental conditions, which can be used as a strategy to control the characteristics and properties of the water-expandable particles.
the use of a low-HLB surfactant, the use of a propeller-type impeller, and a short duration for the water dispersion stage are recommended for the synthesis of water expandable polystylene.
the water droplets are not incorporated into polystyrene by a simple process of mixing the water and polystyrene phases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
water expandable polystyrene can be produced in a controlled manner, which is a key step towards the use of water-expandable PS in the production of lightweight foams.

the use of a surf actant with a low value of the HLB, the use of an anchor-type impeller, and the control of the duration of the dispersion phase of the water are important factors for obtaining water droplets of small size and narrow distribution in the polystyrenes.
the water droplet size is a function of the water dispersion time and the type of the impeller used.
